content.title: Unions: More Than One Valid Possibility
content.context:
- waiting
- working
- finished

Instead of using an arbitrary string, TypeScript can describe the exact allowed values:

```ts
type TaskState = "waiting" | "working" | "finished";
```

That `|` means **or**.

The value must be one of the listed possibilities.
goals: Represent values that intentionally allow more than one possibility using union and literal types.

content.question:
Which assignment is invalid?

```ts
type Theme = "light" | "dark";
```

feedback.correct: `Theme` allows only the two listed string values.
feedback.incorrect: `Theme` allows only the two listed string values.

content.title: Unions of different types
content.text:
A union does not have to list literal strings.

```ts
type Id = number | string;
```

That means an `Id` can hold either a number or a string.

The important catch is that your code must now account for both possibilities when the operation differs.

options.text: `number | string` is not a valid type.
`toFixed` is available on numbers but not guaranteed on every value in the union.
Strings cannot be passed to functions.
The function has too many parameters.

feedback.correct: The type says `id` might be a string. The function cannot safely call a number-only method until it has proved the value is a number.
feedback.incorrect: The type says `id` might be a string. The function cannot safely call a number-only method until it has proved the value is a number.

activities.title: Literal unions are small state machines

content.title: Literal unions are small state machines
content.text:
Consider:

```ts
type SaveState = "idle" | "saving" | "saved" | "error";
```

This is useful because the codebase now has a named, finite vocabulary for the state.

A random string like `"savng"` is no longer silently acceptable.

options.text: A misspelled state name that is outside the allowed set.

feedback.correct: The literal union acts like a small controlled vocabulary.
feedback.incorrect: The literal union acts like a small controlled vocabulary.

content.question:
Why is this often more useful than `string`?

```ts
type Role = "admin" | "editor" | "viewer";
```

options.text: It tells the checker the valid possibilities are limited to a known set.
It removes the need for functions.

feedback.correct: The type records the allowed vocabulary, which lets TypeScript catch values outside that vocabulary.
feedback.incorrect: The type records the allowed vocabulary, which lets TypeScript catch values outside that vocabulary.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A union is a promise that a value belongs to one of several known possibilities.
**Senior habit:** When a value has a small meaningful vocabulary, encode the vocabulary instead of accepting arbitrary strings.
